summary: Sullivan Hill lookout, Crawford County, Mo.: 1941 wooden tower reported; 1956 NGS describes a 50 ft steel tower; listed as removed.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower with a six-foot square platform and guard rail
facts.status_note: Listed as removed on the Forest Lookouts page; no date given.

events.note: Sullivan News item, August 1941: a second wooden tower under construction at Sullivan by CCC 2728. The item names the town, not the hill.
Coast and Geodetic Survey description of the mark: a four-legged steel tower about 50 feet high. First observation of the mark. Does not say whether this is the 1941 tower.
Listed as removed on the Forest Lookouts page; no date given.

evidence.quote: A second wooden tower is under construction by CCC 2728 at Sullivan and others may be built if the war-created steel shortage continues.

corrections.why: NGS datasheet HC0743 gives NAD 83(1997) latitude 37 47 30.92178 N for the tower's survey mark, about 1.7 km north of the brief's value. The NGS description says the station is at the center of the tower.
NGS datasheet HC0743 gives NAD 83(1997) longitude 091 14 25.30418 W for the same mark, about 1 km west of the brief's value.

sources.title: Datasheet HC0743, SULLIVAN HILL LOOKOUT TOWER

notes_for_editor: The 1941 item names the town of Sullivan, not the hill; the link to this tower depends on the Forest Lookouts page. The 1941 wooden tower and the 1956 steel tower are not reconciled: the story says the sources do not show whether they are the same structure. The brief lists Mark Twain National Forest; the only agency text read (NGS 1956) says Clark National Forest, and the later merger was not checked in a fetched page, so the brief's agency is left as is. The main finding is the coordinate correction: the brief's point is about 2 km from the NGS mark, which sits at the tower center. Removal is a bare 'Removed' label with no date. No access, visit or staffing information was found; web search found no tower-specific history. The MDC 'Shooting the Smoke' page is used only for general context.
